gaps.sentence: During the tour she pointed ___ the oldest house in town.
gaps.explanation: point out = mention/draw attention to a fact.

gaps.sentence: A sales rep will follow ___ your enquiry next week.
gaps.explanation: follow up = take further action after something.

gaps.sentence: An accident held ___ the traffic for two hours.
The factory laid ___ two hundred workers.
gaps.explanation: lay off = dismiss workers because there is not enough work.

gaps.sentence: They've just moved ___ to their new flat.
gaps.explanation: move in = start living in a new home.

gaps.sentence: I'm really looking forward to ___ you again soon.
gaps.explanation: look forward TO + -ing: 'to' is a preposition here.

gaps.sentence: The new stadium made ___ an impressive sight.
gaps.explanation: make for = produce a particular result (make for a good atmosphere); also move towards.

gaps.sentence: The ministry tried to play ___ the incident.
gaps.explanation: play down = make something seem less important (opposite: play up).
